definitions.definition: Xn=ℝ^n with the standard orthonormal coordinates indexed by j=1,…,n, its Euclidean norm and inner product, and its standard topology.

Ym=ℝ^m with its standard Euclidean norm |y|=sqrt(Σ_k y_k²) and real inner product ⟨y,z⟩=Σ_k y_k z_k; k runs from 1 to m. All inner products and vector norms below use the corresponding standard real Euclidean structures.

dx is standard Lebesgue measure on Xn=ℝ^n; ∫_{ℝ^n} f(x) dx denotes its real Lebesgue (Bochner) integral. Integrable means absolute Lebesgue integrability. Totalized integrals used for representation assert no finiteness without a proof.
Ω={(x,t)∈Xn×ℝ : t>0}. Positive-time differentiation means ordinary differentiation in this open domain, with no assertion at t=0.
ũ(x,t)=u(x,t) when t>0 and ũ(x,t)=q when t≤0. This only specifies a total representation of u; no regularity at nonpositive times is asserted.

For real normed spaces A,B, a function f:A→B, a point z∈A and a direction v∈A, write D_v f(z)=Df(z)[v]=fderiv ℝ f z v. Here Df(z) is the continuous linear Fréchet derivative when it exists, and the total fderiv convention gives the zero continuous linear map otherwise. This notation alone asserts no differentiability.

b_std is the standard orthonormal basis; its jth vector, written b_j for j=1,…,n, has jth coordinate 1 and other coordinates 0. Fin n indices 0,…,n−1 are an equivalent relabeling with the same Euclidean structures and volume.

definitions.type: family of constant spatial directions in Xn×ℝ

definitions.definition: On Ω set u_t=D_T ũ, u_tt=D_T(D_T ũ), ∂_{x_j}u=D_{S_j}ũ, ∂_{x_jx_j}u=D_{S_j}(D_{S_j}ũ), and ∂_{x_j}u_t=D_{S_j}(D_T ũ). For any scalar or vector field h on Ω use the same total extension convention (arbitrary off Ω) and write ∂_t h=D_T h and ∂_{x_j}h=D_{S_j}h on Ω. These are derivatives of the original germs wherever differentiable. Δ_xu=Σ_{j=1}^n ∂_{x_jx_j}u componentwise, and |D_xu|²=Σ_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u|² is the Frobenius square.

binders.type: scalar or vector field on Ω

definitions.definition: For (x,t)∈Ω, e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|²+Σ_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|². The normalization contains no factor 1/2. When a total time function is needed extend e by zero at t≤0.

definitions.type: family of real flux functions on Ω
definitions.definition: flux is the family denoted g_j: for j=1,…,n and (x,t)∈Ω, g_j(x,t)=⟨u_t(x,t),∂_{x_j}u(x,t)⟩. Extend by zero at nonpositive times when total functions are needed.

For t>0, E(t)=∫_{Xn} e(x,t) dx. This definition alone asserts neither integrability nor differentiability. Use the integral of the zero extension of e for a total real-time representation; its restriction is this same energy.

For a scalar or vector function f on a topological space A with a distinguished zero in its codomain, tsupport f is the closure in A of {z : f(z)≠0}. Compact topological support means that this closed set is compact.

binders.type: function on A with zero in its codomain

inputs.statement: Define e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|²+Σ_{j=1}^n |∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|² and g_j(x,t)=⟨u_t(x,t),∂_{x_j}u(x,t)⟩. The real functions e, ∂_t e, g_j and ∂_{x_j}g_j are jointly smooth on R^n×(0,∞). For every t0>0 there exists a compact C⊂R^n such that, for every r∈(t0/2,3t0/2), all these functions vanish at (x,r) whenever x∉C, and their spatial topological supports are contained in C. This conclusion also holds for each inner-product term ⟨u_t,u_tt⟩, ⟨∂_{x_j}u,∂_{x_j}u_t⟩ and ⟨u_t,∂_{x_jx_j}u⟩. Indices j range from 1 to n.

binders.type: compact subset of ℝ^n, existential after t0

inputs.statement: For every t>0 the real spatial functions x↦e(x,t), x↦∂_t e(x,t), x↦g_j(x,t) and x↦∂_{x_j}g_j(x,t) are Lebesgue integrable on R^n for each j=1,…,n. Here e=|u_t|²+Σ_j|∂_{x_j}u|² and g_j=⟨u_t,∂_{x_j}u⟩. Each of the spatial sections of ⟨u_t,u_tt⟩, ⟨∂_{x_j}u,∂_{x_j}u_t⟩ and ⟨u_t,∂_{x_jx_j}u⟩ is also integrable.

Let n be natural, X=R^n with Euclidean Lebesgue measure, F,D:R→X→R, t0∈R, s a neighborhood of t0, and b:X→R. Suppose F(t,·) is almost everywhere strongly measurable for t sufficiently near t0, F(t0,·) is integrable, D(t0,·) is almost everywhere strongly measurable, b is integrable, and for almost every x and all t∈s both |D(t,x)|≤b(x) and HasDerivAt (r↦F(r,x)) D(t,x) t hold. Then D(t0,·) is integrable and HasDerivAt (t↦∫x F(t,x) dx) (∫x D(t0,x) dx) t0.

  [inst_1 : RCLike.{u_2} 𝕜] {E : Type u_3} [inst_2 : NormedAddCommGroup.{u_3} E] [inst_3 : NormedSpace.{0, u_3} ℝ E]
  [inst_4 : NormedSpace.{u_2, u_3} 𝕜 E] {bound : α → ℝ} {F : 𝕜 → α → E} {x₀ : 𝕜} {s : Set.{u_2} 𝕜},
  Membership.mem.{u_2, u_2} (nhds.{u_2} x₀) s →
    (∀ᶠ (x : 𝕜) in nhds.{u_2} x₀, MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable.{u_1, u_3} (F x) μ) →
      MeasureTheory.Integrable.{u_3, u_1} (F x₀) μ →
        ∀ {F' : 𝕜 → α → E},
          MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable.{u_1, u_3} (F' x₀) μ →
            (∀ᵐ (a : α) ∂μ, ∀ (x : 𝕜), Membership.mem.{u_2, u_2} s x → LE.le.{0} (norm.{u_3} (F' x a)) (bound a)) →
              MeasureTheory.Integrable.{0, u_1} bound μ →
                (∀ᵐ (a : α) ∂μ,
                    ∀ (x : 𝕜), Membership.mem.{u_2, u_2} s x → HasDerivAt.{u_2, u_3} (fun x => F x a) (F' x a) x) →
                  MeasureTheory.Integrable.{u_3, u_1} (F' x₀) μ ∧
                    HasDerivAt.{u_2, u_3} (fun n => ∫ (a : α), F n a ∂μ) (∫ (a : α), F' x₀ a ∂μ) x₀

argument.text: Fix tau>0 and define Uwin,Fpar,Dpar as declared. By N002, Fpar and Dpar are jointly continuous on Uwin×Xn after swapping the two coordinates. Smoothness of e gives, for every x∈Xn and r∈Uwin, HasDerivAt (s↦Fpar(s)(x)) Dpar(r)(x) r: the affine time inclusion has derivative T, so D010 identifies its chain-rule derivative with ∂_t e. Every r in Uwin is positive. N004 makes Fpar(r) and Dpar(r) integrable for every such r, and integrability implies almost everywhere strong measurability. In particular Fpar(tau) is integrable and Dpar(tau) is almost everywhere strongly measurable. Uwin is an open neighborhood of tau, so measurability of Fpar(r) holds eventually at tau.

produces.statement: Fpar and Dpar are jointly continuous on Uwin×Xn; for every x∈Xn and r∈Uwin the time curve has derivative Dpar(r)(x) at r. Fpar(r) and Dpar(r) are integrable and almost everywhere strongly measurable for every r∈Uwin. Uwin is a neighborhood of tau.

argument.text: Choose Cwin by N002 at tau; throughout Uwin, both Fpar and Dpar vanish outside this same compact set. Compact subsets of a finite-dimensional Euclidean space are bounded. Thus the absolute values of all finitely many coordinates on Cwin have a finite common bound. Enlarging that bound by 1 gives a positive radius with Cwin contained in its closed coordinate cube; if Cwin is empty, any positive radius suffices.

produces.statement: Cwin is compact, Fpar(r)(x)=Dpar(r)(x)=0 for every r∈Uwin and x∉Cwin, and there exists rho>0 with Cwin⊂[-rho,rho]^n.

argument.text: Choose rho by F002 and define Qbox and Lwin. Each closed bounded coordinate interval is compact; their finite product Qbox is compact in Xn. The interval Lwin is compact and lies in Uwin, since tau>0 gives tau/2<3tau/4≤5tau/4<3tau/2. Thus Lwin×Qbox is compact. By F001, the real function (r,x)↦|Dpar(r)(x)| is continuous on this compact set. Its continuous image is bounded, so a nonnegative real bound exists (also when the set is empty).

produces.statement: Qbox is compact, Cwin⊂Qbox, Lwin⊂Uwin, and there exists beta≥0 such that |Dpar(r)(x)|≤beta for every r∈Lwin and x∈Qbox.

argument.text: Choose beta by F003, and define bdom and Iwin. The closed cube Qbox is measurable and has finite Lebesgue measure (2rho)^n. The indicator multiple bdom is measurable and its absolute integral is beta(2rho)^n<∞, so bdom is integrable. The interval Iwin is an open neighborhood of tau and is contained in Lwin and Uwin. For x∈Qbox and r∈Iwin, F003 gives |Dpar(r)(x)|≤beta=bdom(x). For x∉Qbox, the inclusion Cwin⊂Qbox implies x∉Cwin, so F002 gives Dpar(r)(x)=0=bdom(x). Thus the bound holds for every x and every r∈Iwin, which also implies the single almost-everywhere assertion with all r in this same neighborhood. F001 supplies the time derivative for every x and every r∈Iwin.

produces.statement: Iwin is a neighborhood of tau contained in Uwin. bdom is Lebesgue integrable, and for every x∈Xn and every r∈Iwin, |Dpar(r)(x)|≤bdom(x) and HasDerivAt (s↦Fpar(s)(x)) Dpar(r)(x) r.

argument.text: Apply M002 with spatial measure dx, F=Fpar, D=Dpar, base time tau, neighborhood Iwin and bound bdom. F001 gives eventual section measurability, base integrability and derivative-section measurability; F004 gives the neighborhood, the integrable bound and both universally quantified pointwise conditions, hence their almost-everywhere forms. The theorem concludes integrability of Dpar(tau) and HasDerivAt (r↦∫_{Xn}Fpar(r)(x) dx) (∫_{Xn}Dpar(tau)(x) dx) tau.

By D011 and D013, the integral time function in F005 is exactly the total representation of E, and its restriction to positive times is the desired energy. The section integrability already instantiated in F001 ensures these are finite Lebesgue integrals for times in Uwin, a neighborhood of tau. Dpar(tau)(x)=∂_t e(x,tau) since tau>0. Restriction to the open positive-time domain preserves this derivative, so F005 gives every clause of the claimed output for this tau. The conclusion contains none of Cwin,rho,beta or the auxiliary windows; eliminate their witnesses and universally quantify tau. No behavior at zero is asserted.

F001 gives integrability of Fpar(tau) since tau∈Uwin.
F001 gives integrability, hence almost everywhere strong measurability, of Dpar(tau).
F004 proves |Dpar(r)(x)|≤bdom(x) for every x and every r∈Iwin; therefore it holds for almost every x with the same universal quantifier over r.
F004 proves integrability of bdom using the finite-measure measurable cube.
F004 proves the required HasDerivAt for every x and every r∈Iwin, hence for almost every x and all such r.
